raw: The scaling along Z slightly improved alignment but did not resolve the mispositioning. The issue may lie in the door’s Y-axis offset, as the door still fails to close flush. A small upward translation along the Y-axis might help align the door with the hinge mechanism. I will simulate a Y-translation of +0.03 to test this adjustment.

The door still jams at 50 degrees, indicating the issue may be rotational rather than translational. A small rotation around the X-axis might help align the door’s swing path with the hinge. I will simulate a 3-degree rotation around the X-axis for P1 to test this adjustment.

The rotation around the X-axis did not resolve the misalignment, and the door still fails to close properly. The issue may lie in the door’s hinge-side thickness or its Y-axis offset. Since scaling along the Y-axis might adjust the door’s width to fit the hinge, I will simulate a Y-axis scaling of 1.2 for P1 to test this.

The 6-degree rotation around the Z-axis did not resolve the misalignment, and the door still fails to close properly. Since the issue persists, I will now try a small scaling along the X-axis (1.2 multiplier) to adjust the door’s width and potentially allow smoother hinge motion. This may help the door clear the body and close flush.

The scaling along the X-axis has caused the door to move further away from the hinge, worsening the misalignment. Instead, I will now try a small translation along the X-axis to bring the door closer to the hinge and improve alignment. I will simulate a translation of +0.05 along the X-axis for P1.
